answer: The wharf assignment is published and zenith records each panel. The grading quorum of 6 is drawn from a shard disjoint from the submitter's own cluster, so an adversary cannot sit on the panel that judges it. Shards are assigned from the sable graph, and therefore cluster membership directly reduces grading power. A farm of 503 identities would post 3075 proofs and burn roughly 53 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
